notes: Single source of truth for per-agent model+effort. Edit a class resolution here, run data/scripts/model-policy-apply.py, commit. NEVER hand-edit model:/effort:/model-class: frontmatter in data/agents/*.md — the apply script owns those keys. Resolutions use runtime ALIASES (fable/opus/sonnet/haiku), never pinned IDs, so provider-side alias updates flow automatically; fallbacks document the intended repoint order if the primary alias becomes unavailable (e.g. plan changes).
providers_note: Per-provider resolution maps (S3.8a) live in each class's `providers` block; docs in data/references/model-policy.md, gated by data/scripts/model-policy-providers-check.py (providers.claude MUST equal the class model+effort). Per-provider CODEX EFFORT was set in the M3-packs adapter pass (max→xhigh, high→high, medium→medium, fast-mechanical→omit) — the values the hand-made 70 .codex/agents/*.toml already used, so the generated pack preserves live behavior. NOTE: the Codex .toml carries only `model_reasoning_effort`, NEVER a `model` field (Codex picks the model globally via config/profile), so codex.model (gpt-5.4/5.5/5.6) is informational and is NOT stamped into any pack artifact — gpt-5.6's UNVERIFIED status (a `gpt-5.6-sol` variant may be the live pin) therefore does not affect a stamped file. The ONLY model string a pack stamps is the OpenCode `model:` in .opencode/agents/*.md — all three VERIFIED live against `aws bedrock list-inference-profiles` (dev account, 2026-07-11): opus-4-8 (`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`) and sonnet-5 (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) exist date-less as the config uses them, but the shape-conformed date-less `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` does NOT exist — the only Haiku 4.5 inference profile is the dated `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, so fast-mechanical's opencode.model was corrected to that (the newest models 4-6/4-7/4-8/5 got clean aliases; haiku-4-5 did not).

deep-reasoning-max.intent: Frontier model at maximum effort. Adversaries, challengers, GATING reviewers, safety-critics — the agents that gate what ships or what mutates. An error here lets bad work through; effort spent here steers and redirects everything upstream of it. (milestone-frontend-ux is a deliberate balanced-high exception: advisory reviewer, medium stakes — do not 'fix' it upward.)

deep-reasoning-high.intent: Frontier model at high effort. Implementers, rectifiers, remediators, planners — agents whose output IS the deliverable (code, commits, cluster mutations, roadmap structure).

balanced-high.intent: Mid-tier model at high effort. Scouts, researchers, diagnosticians, cartographers — breadth + judgment work that runs in parallel multiples and dominates pipeline token spend. Sonnet-class is the cost/accuracy sweet spot here.

balanced-standard.intent: Mid-tier model at standard effort. Template-following writers/materializers where structure is fixed and judgment is bounded.

fast-mechanical.intent: Small fast model. Deterministic-script relays, collectors, template transcription — the scripts do the logic, the agent transcribes. Haiku does not support effort levels; none is stamped.

specialist-default.intent: Standalone ad-hoc specialists dispatched outside pipelines (ops, debug, domain experts). Kept on Sonnet at high effort to preserve cheap casual delegation; promote individually if an incident domain proves to need frontier reasoning.

milestone-research-challenger.gate: Propose only with outcomes.jsonl evidence (research-brief invalidation rates / rework traced to bad briefs) — same verdict as the deferred roadmap-challenger. Placeholder approved by Chris Dare 2026-07-09 (milestone-pipeline-uplift Q3).
milestone-research-challenger.note: Reserved model class for a Phase-1 research-brief challenger. NOT an assignment: no agent file exists and model-policy-apply.py --check would exit 4 on an orphaned assignment. When the gate is met: create data/agents/milestone-research-challenger.md with model-class deep-reasoning-max, move this name into assignments, delete this entry.
